narrative: PC §290.46(j)(4)(A) does not create a $25,000 minimum: it permits actual damages, an additional amount of at least $250 up to three times actual damages, attorney's fees, and exemplary damages or a civil penalty up to $25,000. ICRAA §1786.50, if established, separately uses actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater (except class actions), plus costs/fees and potentially punitive damages for grossly negligent or willful violations. Because Plaintiff remains pro se, his own time is not modeled as accrued recoverable attorney fees. The Amazon position is seasonal/part-time, limiting wage exposure; present valuation should therefore remain conservative until the actual Accurate report and Amazon decision record establish whether registry/criminal-history information caused the lost shift and whether the Fair Chance Act procedures were triggered.
risk: Evidence-dependent on both the §290.46 and Fair Chance Act theories. Lerma v. Amazon.com Services, LLC et al., No. 8:22-cv-01727 (C.D. Cal.), is the central caution: its Megan's Law claim was dismissed because Accurate's own report showed ordinary court-record sourcing and a 'NO RECORD FOUND' sex-offender search; only the unchallenged Fair Chance Act claim remained before the confidential 2023 settlement. Matter 29 still lacks its own actual Accurate report and a confirmed formal adverse-action basis. The disappearance of the assigned shift is concrete evidence of a practical employment loss, but it does not by itself prove registry use or that Amazon considered criminal history in a way triggering the Fair Chance Act's individualized-assessment duties. Discovery should obtain screening Y94611404, every component/source field, Accurate adjudication codes, Amazon-facing status/timestamps, the shift-removal reason, and Amazon's decision audit trail. Under Mendoza, Accurate has a substantial §290.46 defense if it merely reproduced/transmitted information; FCRA/ICRAA are the more natural vendor theories unless discovery shows Accurate itself adjudicated, suppressed, held, or otherwise acted on the registry information. Lerma is notice/history, not a prior §290.46 settlement or willfulness admission. State §425.115 sets nothing federally — FRCP 54(c) controls.
